newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-Santos yr result seen better.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-Santos yr result seen better.

text.p: Oil and gas producer Santos Ltd is expected to post an improvement in earnings for calendar 1996 on Wednesday, but analysts are forecasting a flat 1997 ahead of big earnings growth in 1998.

Forecasts for Santos' 1996 net profit before abnormals ranged from A$154 million to A$189 million, according to BZW's Barceps forecasting survey of 14 analysts, which produced a median of A$163.7 million.

Analysts contacted by Reuters, who did not want to be named, also forecast wide-ranging results, complicated by the treatment of foreign exchange movements which Santos reclassified as a normal component of operating profit in its half year results.
Santos reported a net profit of A$150.1 million in 1995, and an half year net profit of A$88.6 million to June 30, 1996, compared to A$18.5 million in the previous corresponding period.
One analyst, forecasting A$161 million net profit before abnormals, and excluding the company's foreign exchange position, said it would be a lacklustre result.
"Nothing special compared to other companies like Woodside and Oil Search, struck on a four percent increase in sales volume compared to Woodside which was up 17 percent," he said.
Like other analysts, he is forecasting a flat result for 1997, at around A$155 million, jumping to about A$220 million in 1998 when production turns on at the Stag and Elang/Kakatua fields.

Another analyst agreed the 1996 result would be fairly average, forecasting a net profit of A$166 million in 1996, rising to A$190 million in 1998, saying the company grew slowly compared to a Woodside, partly due to its reliance on gas.
He said Santos had been buying growth up until now, such as with its A$200 million 1996 acquisition of Parker and Parsley's Australian assets.
"That has basically supported their earnings for the year,"

However, another analyst, forecasting a net profit of A$178 million before abnormals, which includes foreign exchange movements, said 1996 had been a good year for Santos with record production and revenue, a trend which would continue up to 2000.
He said 1997 revenue looked fairly flat, with oil production expected to decline and gas to rise.

"What this year will be the test of the fruits of their upgraded exploration program, something which will not obviously turn into revenue and production this year but that could have a material effect on sentiment and valuation," he said.

Another analyst, forecasting A$173.2 million before abnormals and including foreign exchange earnings, was also upbeat, saying he believed Santos would "keep on going, steady as she goes", noting its dividend yield was one of the standouts of the energy sector.
"They have such good long-term gas contracts, the future for them is looking pretty healthy, even with the deregulation of the gas industry, because of their size," he said.
